label: 2026 Q3 (Jul–Sep)
asOf: close of $178.44 on 2 Nov 2026, $171.52 after hours (Investing.com)
headline: Revenue doubled and margins hit 62%, yet the stock fell after hours: the good news was already in a 120-plus P/E

points.t: US commercial revenue of $984M passed US government's $953M for the first time; existing customers spent 65% more than a year ago (net dollar retention 165%).
Adjusted operating margin was flat with last quarter rather than still rising; stock compensation was $319M in the quarter.
Total contract value signed this quarter was $2.92B, only 6% above a year ago; US commercial remaining deal value grew just 4% q/q versus 27% last quarter.

reaction: Stock: closed at $178.44 (−3.1%) on report day and fell to $171.52 (−3.8%) after hours. Revenue, profit and full-year guidance all beat, but at the close the market value was about $459B, 63 times trailing revenue and 125 times adjusted earnings. Before the report, consensus cited by TIKR had 2027 revenue at about $12.4B (+45%); the market wanted faster. Slower new contract signings were the question analysts kept returning to. Next-day close to be added. Consensus from Investing.com: EPS $0.41, revenue $2.17B.

segments.title: Revenue mix
segments.take: Almost all growth came from the US, roughly half each from US commercial and US government; international grew only 20–30%.

rows.why: 686 US commercial customers, up 29%; $1.46B of US commercial contracts signed this quarter. Management says customers start with “sovereign AI” bootcamps, then expand quickly from small first contracts.
Maven has over 100,000 users; the Army TITAN prime agreement (eight systems) is being delivered. This revenue depends on the defense budget.
Mainly NATO and allies such as the UK.
Barely grew quarter on quarter. Businesses outside the US haven't caught up.

segments.note: Year-ago international figures are backed out from the growth rates the company gave, accurate to about ±$0.01B.

extras.title: Where it sits in the AI loop
extras.take: Palantir sits at the very end of the chain: when businesses pay for AI, which application does the money land in. It doesn't sell compute or build frontier models; it plugs other people's models into customers' own data and workflows. The same week ServiceNow fell 27%, Palantir kept accelerating: AI isn't replacing it, it's bringing it customers.

items.w: Partners named on the call include NVIDIA, Anthropic and OpenAI. The pitch is “sovereign AI”: customers fine-tune open-weight models (such as NVIDIA's Nemotron) on their own data and run them inside Palantir's Ontology. The cheaper and more plentiful models get, the better for Palantir.
Net dollar retention rose 8 points in a quarter; the top 20 customers averaged $146M each over the past year, up 76%.

In late October ServiceNow fell 27% the next day on fears AI will replace seat-priced software, and Salesforce chose to partner with Anthropic. Palantir isn't priced per seat; it grows with deployments and usage, so it hasn't taken that hit.
Only $30M of equipment purchases in nine months and a 53% free cash flow margin. Next to Google, Amazon and Meta this week, it's one of the few AI companies actually generating cash.
US government is 41% of revenue. Karp's shareholder letter discussed an “anti-war movement”; asked about the impact on government business, management didn't answer directly.

extras.title: Where growth comes from
extras.take: Growth relies on both the number of US business customers and spending per customer rising. The real variable is new contracts: signing growth has dropped from triple digits to single digits, while the stock assumes many years of rapid growth.

items.w: 686 US commercial customers. Management says demand exceeds its staffing, but customer growth is well below revenue growth: most growth comes from existing customers spending more.
Net dollar retention of 165% is among the highest since listing. Contracts start small and expand fast, which is how revenue keeps growing about 20% a quarter.

Total contract value signed was $2.92B versus $2.76B a year ago; remaining deal value $13.4B, up 2% q/q; RPO $4.9B, flat. Revenue is accelerating while the backlog slows, and the two can't diverge forever.
No multi-year targets and no 2027 guidance yet. Full-year revenue guidance has been raised three times this year, from about $7.19B in February to $8.53B now, about 19% higher.

Watch for new contracts and RDV flat for two quarters, net dollar retention falling, US government revenue slowing on budget or politics, and customers going straight to model companies' products instead of Palantir.

trends.why: Nearly doubled in five quarters; Q4 guide adds another 15%
2.5x in a year, now ahead of US government
Flat with last quarter, a 53% margin

valuation.take: Expensive on any current measure: 63 times trailing revenue, 125 times adjusted earnings, 111 times free cash flow. The price rests on many years of rapid growth; if growth falls from doubling to 40–50%, the multiple has to come down a lot.

scenarios.sub: Starting from the 2026 revenue guide midpoint of $8.532B
head: Case
Revenue growth

scenarios.note: Bear: slower signings feed into revenue and margins slip as hiring rises; base: a bit above the pre-report consensus of about $12.4B of 2027 revenue (+45%), with today's margin; bull: this year's growth continues. EPS = revenue × margin × 80% ÷ 2.62B shares (with dilution). These assumptions are ours and are not forecasts.

pricezone.sub: 2027 adjusted EPS × our P/E; price at the 2 Nov close (before the report)
pricezone.why: The price is above the base case: buying now, the base case loses about 8% and the bear case about 51%; only the bull case leaves about 41% of upside. Near the $110 midpoint the base case gains about 49% and the bear case loses about 21%, a reward/risk of about 2.3; the $95 low end is close to the bear-case price. Our 45–90x multiples are far above software peers but below its own 100x-plus forward P/E of the past year: when growth falls from doubling to 50%, the multiple usually falls first.

history.title: Against its own past 5 years
history.sub: Price/sales (TTM revenue, diluted shares), quarter ends
history.note: About 63x now, above 13 of the past 20 quarter ends, against a median of about 24x. It reached 120x in mid-2025 and was only 7x at the end of 2022. We calculate it from SEC revenue, diluted shares and quarter-end closes.

cash.title: Cash generation
cash.sub: Adjusted free cash flow per quarter, $B
cash.note: Nine-month operating cash flow was $3.32B with $30M of capex. Stock compensation was $319M in the quarter, plus $23M of related employer taxes, about 15% of revenue, which adjusted profit doesn't deduct. Receivables rose $843M over the year with revenue.

valuation.next: Next report around early February 2027, with full-year 2027 guidance.
